name: The Bourrassa household — a name the town's own records carry
head: bourrassa_leon

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. church_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 2 July 1835 and nothing says when they came. THE BOUND FALLS AFTER THE SCENE DATE and the record says so rather than narrowing it: the earliest source that names this person is later than 1 July 1835, so they may have arrived after the day this scene models. present_on_scene_date is `uncertain` for that reason.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1835-07-02 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THE SEASON AND NOTHING ELSE. No trade is recorded for this household and no source says why it came; the only thing the evidence gives is when it was here by. This states the draws that were operating in that season and chooses among them nowhere. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

lives_at.note: Not attested: the lists that name this person give no address. The placement sweep assigns homes once the resident list is complete (T-0514, the owner's own sequencing) and this pass will not guess one.

last_dated_appearance.note: NO DATED EVIDENCE AT OR BEFORE 1835-07-01. The earliest date this card carries is 1835-07-02, which is after the scene, so it is a later appearance rather than the leg under this verdict — T-1159 class R5 is where a later record is back-projected, and it is not done here.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE RECORD DOES NOT REACH THE DAY. Every source that names this person falls on one side of 1 July 1835, and nothing follows them to it or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

kin.note: THE MIRROR OF THE ROW ON hh_baptist_john. THE BURIAL ENTRY NAMES THE FATHER, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT IS CLAIMED. Death entry 5 of Father St Cyr's page, Chicago, 2 July 1835: 'On the 2nd of July 1835, I performed the ecclesiastical burial according to the rites of the Catholic Church on the corpse of John Baptist, son of Leon Bourrassa, 28 days old.' Filed as st_cyr_death_05_1 (decedent) and st_cyr_death_05_2 (parent), and both cards were minted from those two rows and carry their record ids, so no identification is being made by name here. THE CHILD WAS ALIVE ON THE SCENE DATE: 28 days old at a burial on 2 July 1835 puts his birth about 4 June 1835 and his death the day AFTER 1 July 1835, so the father and son of this row are father and son in the scene. WHAT THE ENTRY DOES NOT SETTLE: 'John Baptist' is the transcription's reading of the child's name and it is very likely the forename Jean Baptiste standing where a surname was expected — the card is filed under Baptist because that is how the printed register reads, and T-0721 is where names read out of a printer's smudge are ruled on. The RELATIONSHIP does not turn on which of the two the child was called.

sex_basis.note: A DRAW, NOT A READING. Nothing about this person says which sex they were: T-1303 refused the name and was right to. This value is drawn from the measured male share of the roll the person was named on, seeded by their own id so the draw reproduces - retype 'bourrassa_leon:sex_ratio' and the same face comes up. It carries no weight as evidence about this person and it is never promoted. The rate is a ceiling rather than a point reading, because the forename table that settled the rest was built mostly on men's names.

basis.note: Drawn from the 1840 Chicago schedule's column 'free white males 50 under 60', one of its male bands, conditioned on `named_on_a_roll_15_and_over` because the person is named in their own right on any other roll this layer was minted from - a letter list, a subscription, a court docket, a trade notice - or carries a role, a trade, a marriage or a parenthood.

replaceable_by.match: a source that states this person's age, their birth year, or an interval either can be read out of

age_band.note: AN AGE BAND, NEVER A YEAR. No source this project holds bears on when this person was born, so the band is drawn from the only committed sex by age distribution the project has - the 1840 Chicago schedule, five years after the scene and a town twice the size - seeded by this person's own id ('bourrassa_leon:age_bands_1840'). AND THE CONDITIONING IS THE MODEL'S, NOT A SOURCE'S: that a roll naming a person in their own right names somebody 15 or over. The 1840 schedule counts a child as a tally inside a household and never as a correspondent; 15 rather than 20 because an apprentice or a journeyman stands on a trade roll. No source states this rule. No exact year is written, because a year drawn from a decadal band would read as a record of a birth.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE CONSOLIDATED CIVIC, CHURCH, PRESS, BOOK AND CENSUS EVIDENCE (T-0513, T-0514). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.
